notes.text: Now — I will record it to be a witness for God, and against you, as Moses did his song, Deut. xxxi, 19; xxxii, 1. To - To the Lord of the vineyard. Of my beloved - Not devised by me, but inspired by God. Vineyard - His church. Hill - Hills being places most commodious for vines.
He gathered — He removed all hindrances, and gave them all the means of fruitfulness. A tower - For the residence of the keepers.

Nor digged — Vine-dressers use to dig up and open the earth about the roots of the vines. The meaning is, I will remove my ministers, who used great care and diligence to make you fruitful. Thorns - I will give you up to your own lusts. No rain - I will deprive you of all my blessings.
Pleasant — In whom God formerly delighted. A cry - From the oppressed, crying to men for help, and to God for vengeance.

glossa.text: *I will sing to my beloved,* etc. ((HIER.)) A canticle is sometimes in gladness, sometimes in sorrow, as this one is, namely the one which he composed who, seeing the city, wept, saying: *For if thou also hadst known,* etc. ((Luc. XIX)).

*A chosen vineyard.* ((ID.)) Another edition, the vineyard Sorec, which is a kind of the best vine, most fruitful with unfailing fruits; all the things that are said of the vineyard are referred to the state of the soul, which, planted by God, brought forth not grapes but wild grapes: and it was handed over to the beasts to be trodden down, nor did it receive the rain of doctrine, because it despised the gifts that had gone before.
*Now therefore, O inhabitants,* etc. In like manner Nathan questions David, that he may pronounce sentence upon himself as though upon another.
*Is it that I looked for,* etc.? This, according to some, he said above within himself; but here he asks others what he had been thinking.

*And now I will show you.* As if he should say: Because you will not answer, therefore I will answer for you.

 *I will take away,* etc. That is, that they who have not felt God through benefits may feel him through punishments; and therefore he threatens a penalty, that they may be turned to repentance.
*And the clouds.* ((ID.)) Which under Elias, etc., *as far as* when they had not the prophets, and drove the apostles away.

*The house of Israel,* etc. ((ID.)) From the time the kingdom was divided, etc., *as far as* because Christ was born of them.

*Behold a cry.* Wherewith it cried out against the Lord and shouted, saying: Away with him, away with him, crucify him; or, they made a cry in place of justice, because they slew Christ, whose blood cries to the Lord: *The voice of the blood sanguis of thy brother Abel crieth to me from the earth ((Gen. IV))*.

notes.text: Joseph — The children of Joseph or Israel. The name of Joseph, the most eminent of the patriarchs, is elsewhere put for all the tribes. Cherubim - Which were by the mercy seat above the ark.

Before Ephraim — Here is an allusion to the ancient situation of the tabernacle in the wilderness, where these tribes were placed on the west-side of the tabernacle, in which the ark was, which consequently was before them.

glossa.text: *Thou that rulest,* etc. ((AUG.)) Here Asaph, enlightened, speaks of the coming of Christ, who converts man, and makes firm the vineyard brought out of Egypt: this is the testimony for them that are changed. ((CASS.)) Above he was fearful, who was praying for the sins of the Synagogue: now he presumes, and to those changed for the better he gives a testimony. This psalm is the testimony of the Synagogue concerning the head himself, and his body. ((ID.)) A prayer for the first coming, through which the reparation of the human race is made. ((ID.)) Being finished, he makes an end. O God, O Son. *Thou that rulest,* spiritually, *Israel,* who see thee, *Give ear,* that is, pour the light of goodness upon us, that we may be bright from thee, who of ourselves are dark. *Joseph.* ((ID.)) Thou leadest the faithful people into the folds of God, as sheep to the pastures, of whom: *And other sheep I have that are not of this fold, and them I must bring, that there may be one fold and one shepherd ((Joan. X))*. Each has its own proper word: Israel *is ruled,* Joseph *is led,* that is, the devout people. *Be made manifest.* ((ID.)) He asks that he who was in the secret of majesty may appear before the Jews through the incarnation, as it had been promised, working in them these powers which are signified by these names, Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasse. ((AUG.)) *Be made manifest before.* Known to the angels, be made known to men.

*Before Ephraim.* ((AUG.)) That is, in the nation of the Jews, where these tribes are, namely before fruitfulness, and before the son of the right hand, that we also may be the fulness of knowledge through charity, which is God; and before Manasse, that is, the forgotten one, that thou mayest now come into his mind, according to that saying: *All the ends of the earth shall remember, and shall be converted.* ((ID.)) *Stir up.* He repeats, etc., *as far as* crucified through weakness, rise again through power. ((CASS.)) *Stir up thy power* of miracles, etc., *as far as* whence: *God is faithful, who suffereth you not to be tempted above that which you are able,* etc. ((I Cor. X)).

notes.text: They — Moses, Aaron, and the Israelites. Passed the Red Sea - It washed the borders of Edom, which signifies red. Thus far the examples are cited from Genesis and Exodus; those that follow are from the former and the latter Prophets.
By the faith of Joshua.
Rahab — Though formerly one not of the fairest character.
After Samuel, the prophets are properly mentioned. David also was a prophet; but he was a king too. The prophets — Elijah, Elisha, &c., including likewise the believers who lived with them.

David, in particular, subdued kingdoms. Samuel (not excluding the rest) wrought righteousness. The prophets, in general, obtained promises, both for themselves, and to deliver to others. Prophets also stopped the mouths of lions, as Daniel; and quenched the violence of fire, as Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. To these examples, whence the nature of faith clearly appears, those more ancient ones are subjoined, (by a transposition, and in an inverted order,) which receive light from these. Jephthah escaped the edge of the sword; Samson out of weakness was made strong; Barak became valiant in fight; Gideon put to flight armies of the aliens. Faith animates to the most heroic enterprises, both civil and military. Faith overcomes all impediments effects the greatest things; attains to the very best; and inverts, by its miraculous power the very course of nature. 2 Sam. viii, 1,&c.; 1 Sam. viii, 9,&c.; 1 Sam. xiii, 3,&c.; Dan. vi, 22; Dan. iii, 27; Jude xii, 3; Jude xv, 19,&c.; Jude xvi, 28,&c.; Jude iv, 14,&c.; Jude vii, 21.

Women — Naturally weak. Received their dead - Children. Others were tortured - From those who acted great things the apostle rises higher, to those who showed the power of faith by suffering. Not accepting deliverance - On sinful terms. That they might obtain a better resurrection - An higher reward, seeing the greater their sufferings the greater would be their glory. 1 Kings xvii, 22; 2 Kings iv, 35
And others — The apostle seems here to pass on to recent examples.

They were sawn asunder — As, according to the tradition of the Jews, Isaiah was by Manasseh. Were tempted - Torments and death are mentioned alternately. Every way; by threatenings, reproaches, tortures, the variety of which cannot be expressed; and again by promises and allurements.
Of whom the world was not worthy — It did not deserve so great a blessing. They wandered - Being driven out from men.
And all these — Though they obtained a good testimony, ver. 2, yet did not receive the great promise, the heavenly inheritance.
God having provided some better thing for us — Namely, everlasting glory. That they might not be perfected without us - That is, that we might all be perfected together in heaven.

Wherefore, being encompassed with a cloud — A great multitude, tending upward with a holy swiftness. Of witnesses - Of the power of faith. Let us lay aside every weight - As all who run a race take care to do. Let us throw off whatever weighs us down, or damps the vigour of our Soul. And the sin which easily besetteth us - As doth the sin of our constitution, the sin of our education, the sin of our profession.

Looking — From all other things. To Jesus - As the wounded Israelites to the brazen serpent. Our crucified Lord was prefigured by the lifting up of this; our guilt, by the stings of the fiery serpents; and our faith, by their looking up to the miraculous remedy. The author and finisher of our faith - Who begins it in us, carries it on, and perfects it. Who for the joy that was set before him - Patiently and willingly endured the cross, with all the pains annexed thereto. And is set down - Where there is fulness of joy.

glossa.text: *They passed through the Red Sea,* etc. So through baptism the faithful pass over, their sins being remitted; the Egyptians, as it were, being drowned with the devil the prince of darkness.
*By the going round of seven days* being completed by the Levites bearing the ark of God, and sounding with brazen trumpets.

*Receiving the spies with peace,* etc. As if: So ought you also, by believing, to receive the two Testaments through the apostles sent by Christ as spies, and so you shall not perish with the unbelievers.

*Of Gedeon.* He, having received the sign of the fleece from the Lord, went against the Madianites with three hundred men, and overcame them by night. *Samson.* He, as is read in the book of Judges, vehemently afflicted the Philistines. *Jephte.* He, when he was going to the battle against the enemies, vowed to the Lord that, if he should obtain a triumph over the enemies, on returning he would offer to God whatever should first meet him: and his daughter met him, whom he immolated.

*Who by faith.* Although he declines to say what each one did, yet he says what certain men wrought by faith. *Renewed promises.* The Apostle says *renewed promises* and not promises, because many promises were made to David, as to Abraham. Wisely he avoids the recital of the histories, lest he prolong his discourse, touching briefly on certain things. For neither was he altogether silent, nor in speaking was he made burdensome, he fled thickness and length, lest he weary the hearer.

*And others were racked,* etc. In those Fathers of the Old Testament there were examples of patience, though rare, from the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, whose blood the Lord says is to be required of those who should persist in the iniquity of their fathers (by whom those men were slain). And in the New Testament, there have not been wanting men strong in temporal happiness, in which we experience the mercy of God.

*Of whom the world was not worthy.* That is, of whose manner of life *the world was not worthy,* and therefore let them not be held cheap for the tribulations they endured: or, they were so cheap in men's eyes that they were thought not to be worthy to stand or to dwell among them. And both they and those before them did not at once receive the promised life, until Christ. Why not, is subjoined:

*God providing some better thing for us.* Inasmuch as he would assume our nature, and would more gloriously rejoice with us. If they held the faith, who so long awaited us and rest, much more let us hold it, who receive it immediately after death.

*And therefore we also.* After the commendation of faith, he returns to that which he had begun, exhorting to patience in many ways, and chiefly by the example of Christ himself. *A cloud.* That is, the multitude of the saints, who are witnesses of faith, who as clouds refresh us by their own example in the heat of tribulations, and rain upon us with their doctrines.

*Who, having joy set before him,* etc. So ought we, eternal joy being set before us and confusion set aside, to run; or, joy of a temporal kingdom being set before him, when the crowds wished to take him by force to make him king, and he would not, because it was the way of humility.

notes.text: I am come to send fire — To spread the fire of heavenly love over all the earth.
But I have a baptism to be baptized with — I must suffer first, before I can set up my kingdom. And how I long to fight my way through all!
Suppose ye that I am come to send peace upon earth — That universal peace will be the immediate effect of my coming? Not so, but quite the contrary. Matt. x, 34.
There shall be five in one house, three against two, and two against three — There being an irreconcilable enmity between the Spirit of Christ and the spirit of the world.

The father against the son — For those who reject me will be implacable toward their very nearest relations who receive me. At this day also is this scripture fulfilled. Now likewise there is no concord between Christ and Belial.

And he said to the people also — In the preceding verses he speaks only to his disciples. From the west - In Judea, the west wind, blowing from the sea, usually brought rain: the south wind, blowing from the deserts of Arabia, occasioned sultry heat. Matt. xvi, 2.
How do ye not discern this season — Of the Messiah's coming, distinguishable by so many surer signs.

glossa.text:
*Fire,* etc. As if he said: Thou wast asking whether I admonish all men, with loins girt and lamps burning, to await the coming of the Lord? But I, who came into the world only for this, that I might kindle men from the desires of the world to heavenly things, will nothing else save that the radiance of this burning may light up all the parts of the world as far as the end of the age, and that it may so blaze in the hearts of the faithful that it be not quenched by any onset of waves or of blasts.

*But I have a baptism,* etc. And that this fire may be able to be kindled in the hearts of the faithful, so that they may be able perfectly to despise all temporal things and themselves also, I must first be baptized with a baptism, that is, be steeped in the anointing of my own blood: for the Spirit would not be given unless Jesus were first glorified. *And how.* So great is the condescension of the Lord that he testifies there to be in him an eagerness for devotion to be poured into us, and for perfection to be consummated in us, and for the passion to be hastened for us: he who, though he had in himself nothing whereat to grieve, was yet straitened by our troubles, and at the time of death put forward a sadness which he had taken on not from the fear of his own death, but from the delay of our redemption. *Until it be accomplished.* He who is straitened as far as the accomplishment is untroubled about the accomplishment, nor is he straitened about it; but rather the death of the body is the loosing of anxiety, not the heaping up of grief.

*Think ye.* How, after the baptism of the passion and after the coming of the fire, the earth is to burn, he says: Because for the faith of Christ the whole world is divided against itself, and every house had faithful and unfaithful, these fighting against the faith, those for the faith.

*In one house.* Each single man is one house, either God's or the devil's. And so a spiritual man is a spiritual house. *Divided.* The first cause is that of religion toward God, the second that of dutifulness toward one's neighbour. For thou oughtest to set human things after divine. Kindred pledges are not therefore to be renounced, but God is to be preferred to all. For indeed the pledges of nature are God's benefits, nor ought the benefit that is received to be loved more than God, by whom the benefit received is preserved. *Three against two.* That is, the son and the daughter and the daughter-in-law, against the father and the mother; and two against three, that is, the father and the mother, where the mother-in-law also is understood, against the son and the daughter and the daughter-in-law.

*And he said.* When he had instructed the apostles also concerning his first coming, intimating what was done in it, and had admonished them concerning the coming to be, how they ought to await it, he turned his discourse to the crowds, among whom were the Pharisees, as Matthew indicates: because, neither believing the first coming to have taken place nor rightly awaiting the second, they were seeking a sign from heaven, tempting him. These therefore he reproves, because if they were willing to attend, they could have from the words of the prophets a sure sign of both comings. *When you see.* Mystically. The cloud rising from the west signifies the flesh of Christ rising again from death, from which time the shower of the Gospel preaching has been poured out upon all lands. The south wind blowing before the heat signifies the lighter tribulations before the judgment.

*A shower cometh.* Literally the sense is plain: they who from the changing of the elements can foreknow the state of the breezes could also know the time of both comings, both from the sayings of the prophets and from the magnificence of his works.

*Hypocrites,* etc. And lest any unlearned men in the crowd, flattering themselves upon their want of skill, should excuse themselves, saying that they knew not the law and the prophets, he adds that they can discern by natural reason either that he who does works which no other had done is above man and is God, or that after so many injustices of the age the just judgment of the Creator will come.

hymns.title: The Lord comes, the Lord comes
Like an ant on a stick both ends of which are burning
Must Jesus bear the cross alone

praise.title: If You Want to Follow Me

echoes.text: For the son dishonors the father, the daughter rises up against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man’s enemies are the men of his own house.
echoes.note: 'The son treats the father with contempt, the daughter rises up against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law'—Micah's portrait of social collapse—is virtually quoted in the household divisions of 12:53. The matching kinship triads (father/son, mother/daughter, mother-in-law/daughter-in-law) make this a high-Volume allusion.

echoes.text: “But who can endure the day of his coming? And who will stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like launderer’s soap; and he will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi, and refine them as gold and silver; and they shall offer to Yahweh offerings in righteousness.
echoes.note: 'Who can endure the day of his coming? For he is like a refiner's fire' grounds 'I came to throw fire on the earth.' The eschatological refining-and-purging fire of the coming Lord gives strong Coherence to Jesus' fire-bringing mission.

echoes.text: “For, behold, the day comes, it burns as a furnace; and all the proud, and all who work wickedness, will be stubble; and the day that comes will burn them up,” says Yahweh of Armies, “that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.
echoes.note: 'The day comes, burning like an oven... it will set them ablaze' reinforces the kindled fire Jesus casts on the earth. Recurrence of Malachi's fire-of-judgment imagery across chapters 3-4 strengthens the allusion.

echoes.text: I will bring the third part into the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will test them like gold is tested. They will call on my name, and I will hear them. I will say, ‘It is my people;’ and they will say, ‘Yahweh is my God.’”
echoes.note: God will 'put this third into the fire, and refine them as one refines silver' divides a remnant by fire and trial. The refining-fire-that-divides motif coheres with both the fire and the division Jesus brings rather than peace.

echoes.text: Now will I show you the truth. Behold, there shall stand up yet three kings in Persia; and the fourth shall be far richer than they all: and when he has grown strong through his riches, he shall stir up all against the realm of Greece. A mighty king shall stand up, who shall rule with great dominion, and do according to his will. When he shall stand up, his kingdom shall be broken, and shall be divided toward the four winds of the sky, but not to his […]
echoes.note: Apocalyptic expectation that the end-times bring conflict rather than tranquility loosely supports Jesus' 'not peace but division.' Faint coherence with the tribulation-before-the-end pattern.

echoes.text: On the seventh time, he said, “Behold, a small cloud, like a man’s hand, is rising out of the sea.” He said, “Go up, tell Ahab, ‘Get ready and go down, so that the rain doesn’t stop you.’” In a little while, the sky grew black with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain. Ahab rode, and went to Jezreel.
echoes.note: The little cloud rising from the sea heralding heavy rain in Elijah's drought account parallels 'a cloud rising from the west... a shower is coming.' The reading-of-cloud-as-rain-sign offers a faint scriptural precedent for weather discernment.

echoes.text: If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth; and if a tree falls toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falls, there shall it be. He who observes the wind won’t sow; and he who regards the clouds won’t reap.
echoes.note: Qoheleth's observation that 'if the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth' and that the wind-watcher fails to act coheres with reading clouds and wind yet failing to read 'this time.' A wisdom echo on weather-signs and discernment.

doctrine.title: Nicene Creed
doctrine.article: the life of the world to come

notes.text: What is the wheat — There is as much difference between my will and their dreams, as there is betwixt the chaff and the wheat.

glossa.text: *I have heard what they said. ((HIER.))* There are many kinds of prophesying, etc., *as far as* and the untameable hearts of tyrants might feel the majesty of the Lord by their own conscience.
*Their dreams which.* There are today dreamers in the Church, who make their own errors the prophecies of the Lord, saying often, *I have dreamed:* against whom it is said, *How long is this,* etc.
*What hath the chaff to do with the wheat?* Beautifully is the doctrine of the heretics compared to chaff, which has no marrow, nor affords any refreshment.

*Are not my words?* Whereas in the former people the prophets lied, etc., *as far as* the Lord therefore threatens that he will come against masters of this sort.

*As fire.* Of churchmen it is written that hammer and axe were not heard in the house of the Lord.

notes.text: Standeth — To observe all that is said or done there. Mighty - Kings or chief rulers. By their congregation he understands all persons whatsoever of this high and sacred order. Judgeth - Passes sentence upon them. The gods - Judges and magistrates are called gods, because they have their commission from God, and act as his deputies.
How long — The psalmist speaks to them in God's name. Accept - By giving sentence according to your respect or affection to the person.

They — The magistrates of whom this psalm treats. Know not - The duty of their place. Nor will - Their ignorance is wilful. Walk on - They persist: it is their constant course. In darkness - In their sinful courses. The foundations - This corruption of the supreme rulers, flows from them to their inferior officers and members.

Have said — I have given you my name and power to rule your people in my stead. All - Not only the rulers of Israel, but of all other nations. Children - Representing my person, and bearing both my name and authority.
Like men — Or, like ordinary men.

Arise — Take the sword of justice into thine own hand. A remonstrance of the designs and endeavours of Israel's enemies, ver. 1-8. A prayer, that God would defeat them, preserve his church, and get himself glory, ver. 9-18. A song or psalm of Asaph.

glossa.text: *A psalm of Asaph.* ((CASS.)) A psalm on the two natures in Christ, in which Christ, or the Prophet speaking, reproaches Asaph himself, that is, the Synagogue, which saw the Lord bodily, and yet did not know him. First he announces that God has stood, and convicts the adversaries: man stands, God discerns. *God hath stood.* Whose part it is not to stand, who filleth heaven and earth, who is within all things not enclosed, outside all things not excluded; but briefly he indicates God as man. *He hath stood.* ((AUG.)) The Son, who was sent to the sheep of the house of Israel; but the spiritual presence of the Godhead, which, being everywhere, does not properly belong to the Synagogue, nor is varied by time. Why he stood there: *Behold, he judgeth gods,* that is, according as he is God, that is, not by merits but by grace he distinguishes the vessels, some unto honour, some unto dishonour. But this he does standing in the midst, whence: *There hath stood one in the midst of you, whom you know not,* whence also here: *They have not known, neither have they understood,* but *the friend of the bridegroom standeth and heareth, and rejoiceth with joy. Of gods.* Whom afterwards he calls *sons of the Most High,* there: *I have said: you are gods, and all of you to the sons of the Most High.* Whence also, *I have brought up children and exalted them, but they have despised me.* They are called sons not only by the grace of the New Testament, but by the grace of the Old, which delivered them out of Egypt.

*How long.* ((AUG.)) This is the voice of him that discerneth: he sent the law and the Prophets, and you resisted; but how long? Did I send Prophets until the coming, and you afflicted them with injuries, or slew them, or consented to those who did this? But since it is not worthy even to speak to those who do such things, you who kept silence, and wished to imitate them, *how long do you judge iniquity, and accept the persons of sinners?* Is the heir also to be slain, who came for you, who for your sake willed to be without a father, as a fatherless child? who for your sake hungered and thirsted, as a needy man, who for your sake was made poor, when he was rich.

*Judge for the needy and the fatherless, justify the poor and the humble.* ((CASS.)) Diapsalma, he admonishes that one should understand Christ to be God, even if he was needy and poor, which he says that they did not do.

*Rescue the poor.* ((AUG.)) He shows that not even those are guiltless who left Christ to the princes, since they were feared on account of their multitude, and could have freed them from the deed, and themselves from consent. ((CASS.)) For he who ceases to withstand when he can, consents.

*They shall be moved.* ((CASS.)) Hence it is plain of whom he had spoken: this sign happened at the crucifixion. Or spiritually, earthly men were moved at that time, so great a miracle being seen; as the centurion, who said: *Indeed this was the Son of God.* ((AUG.)) *All the foundations shall be moved.* As if he should say: through this blindness of Israel, *shall be moved* unto faith *all the foundations of the earth,* that is, the fulness of the Gentiles shall come in. Or, in the death and passion of the Lord the earth was moved. Or *the foundations,* that is, those made happy by abundance of earthly things, shall be moved. Or by wondering that a poor dead man is worshipped. Or by following after him, earthly things being despised. He adds *all,* because there is none who does not wonder, or is not converted. But the kingdom of earthly felicity is pride, against which the humble Christ came, reproaching them whom he wills to make high through humility, in these words: *I have said: you are gods,* you the good: *but you* the evil, *shall die like men.* Or he says to all: *you are gods,* that is, to all I promised heavenly things; *but you as men,* the first men, who sinned by persuasion, and you greater ones as the devil, who by pride sinned.

*I have said.* ((CASS.)) What was set before them? but they perished. *I have said: They have not known, neither have they understood;* yet *I have said.* All receive these promises, if they keep the commandments, that they may be sons, and of God: this to the just; *but you,* this to the wicked.

*Like men.* ((AUG.)) As if: Whereas you are quickly to die, like men, you are not corrected thereby; but like the devil, who dies not in the flesh, you are lifted up, that you may fall: because through diabolical pride they envied the glory of Christ, and the humility of the cross became vile to them. But, that this vice may be healed, there is subjoined in the person of the Prophet: *Arise, O God,* etc., *as one.* The crowd which fell is called one, because it is alike in pride: You shall fall, but:
*Arise, O God.* ((AUG.)) That is, condemn these, because, these being cast off, thou shalt inherit. Or judge the world, because it is thine, and this is: thou shalt inherit.

notes.text: They — Moses, Aaron, and the Israelites. Passed the Red Sea - It washed the borders of Edom, which signifies red. Thus far the examples are cited from Genesis and Exodus; those that follow are from the former and the latter Prophets.

Women — Naturally weak. Received their dead - Children. Others were tortured - From those who acted great things the apostle rises higher, to those who showed the power of faith by suffering. And all these — Though they obtained a good testimony, ver. 2, yet did not receive the great promise, the heavenly inheritance.
God having provided some better thing for us — Namely, everlasting glory. That they might not be perfected without us - That is, that we might all be perfected together in heaven.

Wherefore, being encompassed with a cloud — A great multitude, tending upward with a holy swiftness. Of witnesses - Of the power of faith. Let us lay aside every weight - As all who run a race take care to do. Let us throw off whatever weighs us down, or damps the vigour of our Soul. And the sin which easily besetteth us - As doth the sin of our constitution, the sin of our education, the sin of our profession.

Looking — From all other things. To Jesus - As the wounded Israelites to the brazen serpent. Our crucified Lord was prefigured by the lifting up of this; our guilt, by the stings of the fiery serpents; and our faith, by their looking up to the miraculous remedy. The author and finisher of our faith - Who begins it in us, carries it on, and perfects it. Who for the joy that was set before him - Patiently and willingly endured the cross, with all the pains annexed thereto. And is set down - Where there is fulness of joy.

glossa.text: *They passed through the Red Sea,* etc. So through baptism the faithful pass over, their sins being remitted; the Egyptians, as it were, being drowned with the devil the prince of darkness.
*By the going round of seven days* being completed by the Levites bearing the ark of God, and sounding with brazen trumpets.

*Receiving the spies with peace,* etc. As if: So ought you also, by believing, to receive the two Testaments through the apostles sent by Christ as spies, and so you shall not perish with the unbelievers.

*Of Gedeon.* He, having received the sign of the fleece from the Lord, went against the Madianites with three hundred men, and overcame them by night. *Samson.* He, as is read in the book of Judges, vehemently afflicted the Philistines. *Jephte.* He, when he was going to the battle against the enemies, vowed to the Lord that, if he should obtain a triumph over the enemies, on returning he would offer to God whatever should first meet him: and his daughter met him, whom he immolated.

*Who by faith.* Although he declines to say what each one did, yet he says what certain men wrought by faith. *Renewed promises.* The Apostle says *renewed promises* and not promises, because many promises were made to David, as to Abraham. Wisely he avoids the recital of the histories, lest he prolong his discourse, touching briefly on certain things. For neither was he altogether silent, nor in speaking was he made burdensome, he fled thickness and length, lest he weary the hearer.

*And others were racked,* etc. In those Fathers of the Old Testament there were examples of patience, though rare, from the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, whose blood the Lord says is to be required of those who should persist in the iniquity of their fathers (by whom those men were slain). And in the New Testament, there have not been wanting men strong in temporal happiness, in which we experience the mercy of God.

*Of whom the world was not worthy.* That is, of whose manner of life *the world was not worthy,* and therefore let them not be held cheap for the tribulations they endured: or, they were so cheap in men's eyes that they were thought not to be worthy to stand or to dwell among them. And both they and those before them did not at once receive the promised life, until Christ. Why not, is subjoined:

*God providing some better thing for us.* Inasmuch as he would assume our nature, and would more gloriously rejoice with us. If they held the faith, who so long awaited us and rest, much more let us hold it, who receive it immediately after death.

*And therefore we also.* After the commendation of faith, he returns to that which he had begun, exhorting to patience in many ways, and chiefly by the example of Christ himself. *A cloud.* That is, the multitude of the saints, who are witnesses of faith, who as clouds refresh us by their own example in the heat of tribulations, and rain upon us with their doctrines.

*Who, having joy set before him,* etc. So ought we, eternal joy being set before us and confusion set aside, to run; or, joy of a temporal kingdom being set before him, when the crowds wished to take him by force to make him king, and he would not, because it was the way of humility.

notes.text: I am come to send fire — To spread the fire of heavenly love over all the earth.
But I have a baptism to be baptized with — I must suffer first, before I can set up my kingdom. And how I long to fight my way through all!
Suppose ye that I am come to send peace upon earth — That universal peace will be the immediate effect of my coming? Not so, but quite the contrary. Matt. x, 34.
There shall be five in one house, three against two, and two against three — There being an irreconcilable enmity between the Spirit of Christ and the spirit of the world.

The father against the son — For those who reject me will be implacable toward their very nearest relations who receive me. At this day also is this scripture fulfilled. Now likewise there is no concord between Christ and Belial.

And he said to the people also — In the preceding verses he speaks only to his disciples. From the west - In Judea, the west wind, blowing from the sea, usually brought rain: the south wind, blowing from the deserts of Arabia, occasioned sultry heat. Matt. xvi, 2.
How do ye not discern this season — Of the Messiah's coming, distinguishable by so many surer signs.

glossa.text:
*Fire,* etc. As if he said: Thou wast asking whether I admonish all men, with loins girt and lamps burning, to await the coming of the Lord? But I, who came into the world only for this, that I might kindle men from the desires of the world to heavenly things, will nothing else save that the radiance of this burning may light up all the parts of the world as far as the end of the age, and that it may so blaze in the hearts of the faithful that it be not quenched by any onset of waves or of blasts.

*But I have a baptism,* etc. And that this fire may be able to be kindled in the hearts of the faithful, so that they may be able perfectly to despise all temporal things and themselves also, I must first be baptized with a baptism, that is, be steeped in the anointing of my own blood: for the Spirit would not be given unless Jesus were first glorified. *And how.* So great is the condescension of the Lord that he testifies there to be in him an eagerness for devotion to be poured into us, and for perfection to be consummated in us, and for the passion to be hastened for us: he who, though he had in himself nothing whereat to grieve, was yet straitened by our troubles, and at the time of death put forward a sadness which he had taken on not from the fear of his own death, but from the delay of our redemption. *Until it be accomplished.* He who is straitened as far as the accomplishment is untroubled about the accomplishment, nor is he straitened about it; but rather the death of the body is the loosing of anxiety, not the heaping up of grief.

*Think ye.* How, after the baptism of the passion and after the coming of the fire, the earth is to burn, he says: Because for the faith of Christ the whole world is divided against itself, and every house had faithful and unfaithful, these fighting against the faith, those for the faith.

*In one house.* Each single man is one house, either God's or the devil's. And so a spiritual man is a spiritual house. *Divided.* The first cause is that of religion toward God, the second that of dutifulness toward one's neighbour. For thou oughtest to set human things after divine. Kindred pledges are not therefore to be renounced, but God is to be preferred to all. For indeed the pledges of nature are God's benefits, nor ought the benefit that is received to be loved more than God, by whom the benefit received is preserved. *Three against two.* That is, the son and the daughter and the daughter-in-law, against the father and the mother; and two against three, that is, the father and the mother, where the mother-in-law also is understood, against the son and the daughter and the daughter-in-law.

*And he said.* When he had instructed the apostles also concerning his first coming, intimating what was done in it, and had admonished them concerning the coming to be, how they ought to await it, he turned his discourse to the crowds, among whom were the Pharisees, as Matthew indicates: because, neither believing the first coming to have taken place nor rightly awaiting the second, they were seeking a sign from heaven, tempting him. These therefore he reproves, because if they were willing to attend, they could have from the words of the prophets a sure sign of both comings. *When you see.* Mystically. The cloud rising from the west signifies the flesh of Christ rising again from death, from which time the shower of the Gospel preaching has been poured out upon all lands. The south wind blowing before the heat signifies the lighter tribulations before the judgment.

*A shower cometh.* Literally the sense is plain: they who from the changing of the elements can foreknow the state of the breezes could also know the time of both comings, both from the sayings of the prophets and from the magnificence of his works.

*Hypocrites,* etc. And lest any unlearned men in the crowd, flattering themselves upon their want of skill, should excuse themselves, saying that they knew not the law and the prophets, he adds that they can discern by natural reason either that he who does works which no other had done is above man and is God, or that after so many injustices of the age the just judgment of the Creator will come.

echoes.text: For the son dishonors the father, the daughter rises up against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man’s enemies are the men of his own house.
echoes.note: 'The son treats the father with contempt, the daughter rises up against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law'—Micah's portrait of social collapse—is virtually quoted in the household divisions of 12:53. The matching kinship triads (father/son, mother/daughter, mother-in-law/daughter-in-law) make this a high-Volume allusion.

echoes.text: “But who can endure the day of his coming? And who will stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like launderer’s soap; and he will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi, and refine them as gold and silver; and they shall offer to Yahweh offerings in righteousness.
echoes.note: 'Who can endure the day of his coming? For he is like a refiner's fire' grounds 'I came to throw fire on the earth.' The eschatological refining-and-purging fire of the coming Lord gives strong Coherence to Jesus' fire-bringing mission.

echoes.text: “For, behold, the day comes, it burns as a furnace; and all the proud, and all who work wickedness, will be stubble; and the day that comes will burn them up,” says Yahweh of Armies, “that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.
echoes.note: 'The day comes, burning like an oven... it will set them ablaze' reinforces the kindled fire Jesus casts on the earth. Recurrence of Malachi's fire-of-judgment imagery across chapters 3-4 strengthens the allusion.

echoes.text: I will bring the third part into the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will test them like gold is tested. They will call on my name, and I will hear them. I will say, ‘It is my people;’ and they will say, ‘Yahweh is my God.’”
echoes.note: God will 'put this third into the fire, and refine them as one refines silver' divides a remnant by fire and trial. The refining-fire-that-divides motif coheres with both the fire and the division Jesus brings rather than peace.

echoes.text: Now will I show you the truth. Behold, there shall stand up yet three kings in Persia; and the fourth shall be far richer than they all: and when he has grown strong through his riches, he shall stir up all against the realm of Greece. A mighty king shall stand up, who shall rule with great dominion, and do according to his will. When he shall stand up, his kingdom shall be broken, and shall be divided toward the four winds of the sky, but not to his […]
echoes.note: Apocalyptic expectation that the end-times bring conflict rather than tranquility loosely supports Jesus' 'not peace but division.' Faint coherence with the tribulation-before-the-end pattern.

echoes.text: On the seventh time, he said, “Behold, a small cloud, like a man’s hand, is rising out of the sea.” He said, “Go up, tell Ahab, ‘Get ready and go down, so that the rain doesn’t stop you.’” In a little while, the sky grew black with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain. Ahab rode, and went to Jezreel.
echoes.note: The little cloud rising from the sea heralding heavy rain in Elijah's drought account parallels 'a cloud rising from the west... a shower is coming.' The reading-of-cloud-as-rain-sign offers a faint scriptural precedent for weather discernment.

echoes.text: If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth; and if a tree falls toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falls, there shall it be. He who observes the wind won’t sow; and he who regards the clouds won’t reap.
echoes.note: Qoheleth's observation that 'if the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth' and that the wind-watcher fails to act coheres with reading clouds and wind yet failing to read 'this time.' A wisdom echo on weather-signs and discernment.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Jesus came to bring fire to the earth, and how he wished it were already kindled.
Stir the embers in us, Lord.
You brought a vine out of Egypt and planted it with your own hand.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine, that we may be saved.
So great a cloud of witnesses surrounds us; lay aside every weight.
Let us run the race set before us, eyes fixed on Jesus.
Come, and worship the pioneer of our faith.
We run, and we will not grow weary. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Jesus says he came to cast fire on the earth — not a tame candle, but a blaze he longed to see catch and spread.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
You dug up a vine from Egypt, cleared the ground, and planted it; now you look down the long rows for the fruit of justice.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
And we are not running alone: a great cloud of witnesses fills the stands, those who ran before us and kept the faith.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
So lay down the weight that slows you, feel the fire catch, and run with your eyes fixed on Jesus, who finished the course ahead of us.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine, that we may be saved. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Jesus longs to set the earth on fire.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
You planted us like a vine and tend us still.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
A cloud of witnesses cheers us on the course.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
Lay down the weight; come run and worship.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine. Amen.
